subtitle: Fictional company - illustrative data

slides.title: Nimbus Analytics: Q3 FY25 Business Review
slides.subtitle: Growth, retention and Q4 priorities
slides.speaker_notes: Welcome. This is the Q3 review for the leadership team. Nimbus Analytics is a fictional company and all numbers are illustrative.

slides.title: Q3 beat plan on revenue and retention
bullets: ARR finished 4% above plan, driven by enterprise expansion
slides.speaker_notes: Four numbers to remember. ARR and retention are both ahead of plan, and margin held steady despite heavier infrastructure spend.

slides.title: ARR has grown every quarter for two years
bullets: No quarter below plan since Q1 FY24
slides.speaker_notes: Consistency is the story here. Growth is coming from both new logos and expansion, which makes the trajectory more durable.

slides.title: Expansion now contributes more new ARR than new logos
slides.speaker_notes: For two quarters in a row, existing customers have added more ARR than new customers. That validates the land-and-expand motion.

slides.title: Strong wins, but sales capacity is a constraint
right_bullets: Two senior AE roles still open
Cloud costs up 11% quarter over quarter
slides.speaker_notes: We are winning when we compete, but we are capacity constrained. Hiring and cloud cost control are the two issues to fix in Q4.

slides.title: Q4 priorities focus on capacity and efficiency
bullets: Close both open enterprise AE roles by November
Cut cloud cost per customer 8% through workload rightsizing
Launch partner channel pilot with two system integrators
Ship SSO and audit logs to unblock regulated buyers
slides.speaker_notes: Each priority has a named owner and a measurable target. We will report progress on all four at the next monthly review.

slides.title: Summary
bullets: Q3 ahead of plan: $48.2M ARR, 118% NRR
Expansion revenue is now the main growth engine
Q4 focus: hiring, cloud efficiency, enterprise features
